answer: Global Entry enrollment turns identity into a physical appointment: $120, fingerprints, an FBI background check, and a face-to-face interview at a CBP enrollment center. A hollow file with no passport or travel history is refused at the desk, and one ember of doubt — fingerprints already on file under another name — voids the application and freezes both identities. Forging 1,000 agents means 1,000 passports, 1,000 interviews, and $120,000 in fees, and no script can sit in the chair: the officer keeps a raven’s memory for faces.
